searches.note: Twenty two searches of a share of twenty eight, none the author's. Two searches were restricted to a producer's own domain (kreinbacher.hu, kolonicspinceszet.hu) and read as primary for the house's own dates and methods; one to bor.hu and one to parlament.hu, read as primary. One search, on the Somló and Nagy-Somló names, served all five records. No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules.
What a search contradicted was set right with its source; what rested on one secondary source or none was cut or hedged.
Sources whose title or address names a living person were met among the results and are cited neither in the fragment nor here.

tested: Founding 2002 (first vineyards bought): estate history via retail summaries and Magyar Bor (bor.hu); kept.
Sparkling cellar completed 2011, first release 2014: Bortarsasag, Magyar Bor; kept. The 2011 base wine claim stays out, as the author left it.

Prestige Brut cépage and lees time: kreinbacher.hu (primary, by search) gives Chardonnay the larger part and 36 to 40 months; older retail sheets give mostly or wholly Furmint and 24 to 30 months; the record already says both; kept.
Cellar master from Champagne advising: Magyar Bor and Bortarsasag name him (living, unnamed here); kept.
The 2011 buildings: ArchDaily and AAS Architecture describe a complex hidden in an artificial hill blending with the volcano; the lava flow wording was set right.
The Magyar Bor nineteenth century line was not in Magyar Bor's page and was replaced by what the page says.
Serving 8 to 10 degrees, never decanted, matches the service reference; Brut and Pezsgő label words are plain terms; kept.
changed: story: "by the estate's own account no house on the hill had made sparkling wine fermented in the bottle" was found in no source of this check and is cut; the plan of 2002 stands alone.

story: the 2011 buildings "shaped to echo the lava flows and basalt" was unsourced; now "set into an artificial hill shaped to blend with the slopes of the volcano", as the architects' published project describes it (ArchDaily, AAS Architecture).

story: Magyar Bor setting the house "in the line of the nineteenth century sparkling wine houses" was not in the Magyar Bor page searched; now its actual point, that basalt and Furmint without limestone make sparkling wine (bor.hu, sparkling wine article).

wine.label: Nagy-Somló was glossed as the district "of the hill"; Nagy-Somló is the wider protected name taking in Ság and Kis-Somló beside Somló (Taste Hungary, Vinorandum, the ministry's product specification notice), now said so.
open: Prestige Brut's grape balance has moved: older sheets mostly or wholly Furmint, the estate's current sheet Chardonnay the larger part; the record names both and says so. The plan's why (built on Furmint) should be softened by the read together agent.

tested: 1946: Wine Folly guide, hungarianwines.eu, bor.hu; kept (one account has the old press house bought that year, so "began with a small plot").
Aranyhegy Juhfark oak aged, sold as Selection or Top Selection, labelled Somlói: bor.hu summit and Vinexpo listings, parlament.hu; appellation and label set right.
Grófi as the Hárslevelű site: bor.hu, IWC, Jancis Robinson tasting listings; confirmed, so the author's correction of the plan stands.
Loss of land under collectivisation: one travel blog for, one wine blog against; cut.
The four named vineyards, the museum and the vintage sheet making: not confirmed; cut or reduced.
changed: wine.appellation: was Nagy-Somló; the wine is listed as Tornai Somlói Selection Aranyhegy Juhfark (Magyar Bor's summit and Vinexpo listings on bor.hu, the Parliament page), so now Somló, and the label term Nagy-Somlói is now Somlói.
wine.label: added Selection, the tier the label prints (Top Selection on older labels: the Parliament page and bor.hu listings).

wine.making: the short maceration, gentle pressing, six months on stirred lees rested on one importer's sheet for one vintage; now only what several sources share, fermented and aged in oak, with no time given.
wine.sites and story: the four named vineyards (Grófi, Ilona, Apátsági) were not confirmed; now Aranyhegy and Grófi only, both confirmed by bottlings (bor.hu, IWC, hungarianwines.eu).
story: the family's loss of its land under collectivisation rests on one travel blog and a second blog says collectivised farming never took hold on Somló; cut, the post 1990 growth told generally.
story: the museum beside the cellar was unconfirmed and is cut; the plot "planted" in 1946 is now "began with", since one account has the old press house bought that year.
sources: Wikipedia on Somló replaced by the Parliament page, which confirms the oak aged Aranyhegy Juhfark.
open: The plan's note asks for a Grófi Juhfark; Grófi is the house's Hárslevelű site in every source, so the record teaches the Aranyhegy Juhfark under the plan's key; the read together agent should set the plan's why and note right.
The founder (Endre Tornai) is described, not named: his dates were not found in two sources. The 1982 co-operative and first private bottling story stays out, as the author left it.
The Maria Theresa favour is told as a claim; it was not tested further in this check.

tested: Postmaster great grandfather, graduation gift, first wines 2000, main building 2008: the house's own history page (primary, by search); kept, 2001 replaced by 2008.
Fourth generation: importer profiles; kept.
Six to twelve hours on skins, wild yeast, oak and acacia: Decanter, the Parliament page, Wanderlust Wine, The Wine Society; kept.
Ageing: Parliament a year at least, Wanderlust two to three years; reworded.
2017 Parliament category winner, the wine Somlói Juhfark 2015: parlament.hu; kept and made exact.
Cask names: Álmos confirmed by a Delectable listing; Töhötöm in one listing only, cut.
changed: wine.making: the ageing "about a year, in the cellar's habit of one to three years" is now "at least a year, two to three years by one importer's account": the Parliament page gives a minimum of a year, Wanderlust Wine two to three years.
wine.label: Hordó (cask) was not shown to be printed on a label and is cut; Nagy-Somlói now glossed as the wider district taking in Ság and Kis-Somló (Taste Hungary, Vinorandum).
story: "the house counts 2001 as the year it took its shape" was not borne out by the house's timeline (its 2001 entry concerns a wine); now the main building of 2008, from the same page.

story: the cask names "from figures of Hungarian legend" are now named for chieftains of early Hungarian history, with Álmos (a bottling confirmed in a Delectable listing); Töhötöm, in one retail listing only, is cut from the trap.
story and question: the 2017 Parliament honour now names the winning wine, Somlói Juhfark 2015 (parlament.hu).
open: The winemaker is living and is not named; the house's legal name carries his first name.

tested: Founding: early 1980s by the cellar's Vinitaly page, early 1970s by Wine Anorak and importers; both now given; founded stays empty.
The founder's nickname on the hill, retirement and sale to three partners in 2014: Wine Anorak, Novel Wines, a second importer; kept (one source has after the 2015 vintage, noted open).
Whether the founder is living: no death notice found and recent pieces give his age in his nineties; treated as living, not named.
Making: wild yeast in used Hungarian oak of about a thousand litres, ten to twelve months, then steel; three to four years before release on the house's own page; set to about a year.
Aranyhegy and Szent Márton holdings: the Wines of Hungary Vinitaly sheet, SommSelect for Aranyhegy; kept.
changed: wine.making: "about ten months in used oak casks of a thousand litres" was one vintage's sheet; the importers and the house sheets agree on wild yeast fermentation in used Hungarian oak of about a thousand litres for ten to twelve months, so now "about a year".
story: the start is the early 1980s by the cellar's own page (Wines of Hungary, Vinitaly) but the early 1970s by Wine Anorak and most importers; the story now gives both.

questions[1]: the story question asked the founding decade by the cellar's account, which the sources dispute; it now asks what happened in 2014, the retirement and the sale to partners (Wine Anorak, Novel Wines, a second importer).
open: The founder is living, by every source read (described as in his nineties in recent pieces), and is not named; the three partners who bought the cellar in 2014 are living and not named. One source says the handover came after the 2015 vintage; 2014 is the common date.
A retailer says recent vintages carry Nagy-Somló rather than Somló on the label; the record keeps Somlói, as the house's 2019 sheet has it.

tested: Pannonhalma ownership: the cellar's own history (Substack, by search) gives vines from 1811 and this land bought from the Stern brothers in 1901; the 1911 sale is unclear in every summary; set right.
1948 nationalisation, the cellar to the Fazekas vintner family, the 2001 purchase and more than twenty parcels: the cellar's history, bor.hu, winesofhungary.hu; kept.
Wild yeast, Hungarian oak, sulphur alone: winesofhungary.hu and bor.hu repeat the cellar's words; kept, hedged.
Organic: SommSelect says the vines are farmed organically; the 2017 start is the cellar's alone; hedged.
Zirc: the cellar's history and Offbeat Budapest; kept, named as Cistercian.
changed: story: the abbey's tie was "early in the twentieth century" with "a sale recorded in 1911" and a "Viennese vineyard"; the cellar's own history gives Pannonhalma vines on the hill from 1811 and the purchase of this land in 1901, while the 1911 sale is ambiguous in every summary; now 1811 and 1901 by the cellar's account, the 1911 sale and the Viennese name cut.
story and trap: Zirc now named as the Cistercian abbey, which held Somló land before the war (Offbeat Budapest, the cellar's own history).
questions[1]: the distractor 1911, no longer in the record, is now 1901.
wine.sites: "facing the morning sun" was an inference and is cut; the south-east aspect and more than twenty parcels stand (SommSelect, the cellar's own history).
wine.making: hedged as the cellar's own account; organic farming confirmed by an importer, the year 2017 by the cellar alone.
wine.label: Nagy-Somlói now glossed as the wider district taking in Ság and Kis-Somló.
open: The vintner's grandson, who works in the cellar, is living and is not named; neither is the founding partner of 2001.

appellation_names: Nagy-Somló and Somló are two protected names: Nagy-Somló takes in the hills of Ság and Kis-Somló beside Somló, Somló is the hill alone (Taste Hungary, Vinorandum; a ministry notice of June 2023 records the parallel protection and the growers' wish to keep one name). Every Nagy-Somlói label gloss in the group now says so; Tornai's flagship is labelled Somlói.

swaps.proposal: No producer swap; the author teaches the Aranyhegy Juhfark under the plan's key in place of the plan's Grófi Juhfark.
swaps.why: Grófi is the house's Hárslevelű site in every listing found (bor.hu, IWC, Jancis Robinson tastings) and the Aranyhegy Juhfark is the house's oak aged single vineyard Juhfark (bor.hu, parlament.hu); the read together agent should set the plan's why and note right.

swaps.proposal: Soften the plan's why, built on Furmint.
swaps.why: The estate's own current sheet gives Prestige Brut more Chardonnay than Furmint; the why should say Furmint and Chardonnay.

swaps.proposal: The plan's why calls the house one of the revival after communism.
swaps.ruling: accepted as a correction of the why
swaps.why: The cellar dates itself to the early 1980s and others to the early 1970s, both before 1990.

codex_tension: The Somló region record's summary says the protected name on a label is Somlói and the district's administrative name is Nagy-Somló; both are protected names, Nagy-Somló the wider of the two taking in Ság and Kis-Somló, and several houses label Nagy-Somlói. Reported, not edited.
The region record's producers line calls Tornai one of the largest houses and its range at every price: a size claim and a price word, for the region's own reviewers. Reported, not edited.
